dedupe_keys.name: unjani clinic network south africa solar power water conservation and climate resilience in primary care clinics

description: This case study describes how the Unjani Clinic network, a network of nurse-run primary healthcare clinics in South Africa, has combined climate change mitigation and adaptation in its operations. Harsha Davé published it in The Journal of Climate Change and Health in 2025. Operational data from the network's annual reports and supplier quotes were analysed to evaluate practices such as hybrid or off-grid solar power systems and water conservation. At the time, 19 percent of clinics ran on hybrid or off-grid solar, cutting utility costs by up to 164,512 rand (about 9,139 US dollars) and carbon emissions by 23,000 kg. Flooding and a tornado had seriously disrupted some clinics, underlining the value of emergency preparedness and support from the network. The article is available online, free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial No Derivatives licence. Coverage is the national clinic network. Caveats: savings come from reports and quotes, not metered evaluation, and the clinic-level data are not published. Flexible implementation and leadership support enabled the changes, and the author presents the model as replicable if investment and policy support are aligned. Simulation uses: costs and outage exposure of solar-backed primary care clinics for health facility energy resilience models. Related records: the Pueblo community health centre clinic case (case_study-cr4hc-case-study-pueblo-community-health-center-east-side-clinic) covers climate resilience at a US clinic.
